page: Amazon Web Services c5ad.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 vCPUs, which correspond to 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding 2.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled as a 150 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and baseline network bandwidth is rated at 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reveal a mix of average and weak results. Single-core performance is moderate, with Geekbench single-core and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scoring in the average range. However, multi-core performance is limited, with stress-ng multi-core and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression falling into the bottom 10% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with both small and large block read-only tests categorized as weak, and PassMark memory scores ranking in the bottom 10%. Cryptographic operations show relative strength, with the PassMark CPU encryption test achieving an average rating, supported by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA extensions.

Given the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and the presence of a fast 150 GB local NVMe SSD, this instance offers a specific balance of compute resources and high-speed local storage. It is suitable for workloads that require fast temporary storage but have modest memory requirements, such as basic web serving, light software compilation, or single-threaded data processing. However, the weak multi-core scaling and low memory bandwidth make it less suitable for memory-intensive databases or heavy multi-threaded parallel processing. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of bundled NVMe storage provides value for disk-I/O-bound tasks without requiring external network-attached storage.
